summary: Georgios T. Halkias specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble, he has held posts at SOAS, the Warburg Institute, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Hong Kong.

Gerald B. Kelley worked in linguistics and Indology. After earning his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he served there as an assistant professor from ~1959 to 1963 before becoming a professor at Cornell University in 1963.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig from ~1969 to 1974. He held positions at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989), the University of Göttingen (~1994–2016), and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1994–2016).

Gerald James Larson specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He was a professor at UC Santa Barbara from 1972 and later became Rabindranath Tagore Professor Emeritus at Indiana University Bloomington in 1995.

Gerald Patrick Moriarty was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Pembroke College and Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service, tutored at Oxford, and was University Teacher of Indian History at Cambridge from 1897 to 1924.

Gerald Schwedler is a historian who studied at Heidelberg University. He held posts as a research assistant at the University of Zurich (2015–2018), substitute professor at Konstanz and Heidelberg, and faculty member at Kiel University beginning in 2018.
Gerard Abraham Joseph worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was a member of the Ceylon Civil Service and served as secretary and librarian at the National Museum of Colombo starting in 1893.

Gerard Leslie Makins Clauson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Corpus Christi College, Oxford, he later held a post at the University of Oxford.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Leiden University from ~1908 to 1916, he held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gerasim Stepanovich Lebedev was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Das in 1787. He served as an interpreter at the Collegium of Foreign Affairs in 1801 and worked at the Département asiatique from ~1802 to 1817.
Gerd J. R. Mevissen is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He held appointments at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and in 2026 as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter.
Gerda Hartmann was an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at Kiel University under Friedrich Otto Schrader (~1928–1932). She held a position at the Library of Congress from 1938 to 1940.

Gereon Kopf works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Temple University and mentored by Yasuo Yuasa, he conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan Universities, teaching at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong.

Gergana Ruseva is an Indologist who completed an MA at Sofia University, where she served as a lecturer in 2000 and associate professor in 2012. She was also a physicist at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences from 2000 to 2009.

Gergely Hidas specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Csaba Töttössy, and Ferenc Ruzsa, he held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

Gergely Orosz is a Tibetologist who worked as a librarian at the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (attested 2002). He earned his PhD at the Budapest University of Technology and Economics, becoming an assistant professor there in 2023.

Gerhard Czerny was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Between 1923 and 1927, he studied at the universities of Vienna, Rostock, and Erlangen-Nuremberg under Paul Althaus and Julius von Negelein.

Gerhard Meiser was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the universities of Munich, Belgrade, and Sarajevo, as well as the University of Regensburg (~1971–1979) and the University of Freiburg (~1979–1985).

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Innsbruck, Sorbonne, and under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan, he held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and as professor at the University of Vienna (1964–1997).

Gerhard Wolf is a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Heidelberg University (~1973–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1995–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003).
